text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Europe uses harsh language against Turkey for the lack of progress on the Cyprus problem. United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan hopes for a meeting between Greek Cypriot leader President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in June.
- Police suspect suicide in the death of a soldier at his army quarters on Monday afternoon.
- Annan hopes for three rounds of talks on the Cyprus question by September which could provide an indication on whether progress has been made towards solving the dispute.
- The government plans protests over the forced cancellation of an Easter pilgrimage by Greek Cypriots to Turkish-held Apostolos Andreas monastery in the north of the island.
- The Cyprus Stock Exchange plans to free the fixed trading brokerage commissions to allow stockbrokers to set their fees according to demand and supply.
- Planet Hollywood sets its sights on Cyprus.
- A meeting of the five permanent members at the United Nations on the Cyprus dispute triggers new efforts to promote a solution. Russia's representative submitted a blueprint for a solution.
- Russia intervenes with a document outlining the basic principles for a solution to the Cyprus dispute. The pressure is on from the United States for the two sides to start a direct dialogue.
- Washington mulls over a system of guarantees for Cyprus to broaden the original arrangement between Britain, Turkey and Greece.
